hints: A die throw adds a value from 1 through 6, so the sequence counts satisfy a recurrence using the previous six values.
The target n can be enormous, so a loop up to n is too slow.
Represent the recurrence as a 6-state vector and raise its transition matrix to power n.
analogy: A fixed six-step rule can jump many target values at once by exponentiating its transition.
example: For n=3, the ordered throws summing to 3 are 1+1+1,1+2,2+1,3, so answer 4.
algorithm: Let dp[s]=sum(dp[s-1..s-6]), with dp[0]=1. Build the 6x6 companion matrix for this recurrence and binary-exponentiate it to obtain dp[n] modulo 1e9+7.
correctness: The recurrence partitions ways by the last die result; matrix powers apply this recurrence the requested number of times without computing intermediate states one by one.
complexity: O(6^3 log n) time and O(6^2) space.
